newsitem.title: UK: TLG sees most of its markets stabilising.
newsitem.headline: TLG sees most of its markets stabilising.

text.p: Light fitting group TLG Plc said on Thursday that with the exception of Germany it expects its markets to stabilise during the year.

"Despite market declines in recent years, there are important areas of improvement in the lighting market which we are exploiting," said chairman Hamish Bryce in a statement accompanying annual results.

The group announced that pretax profits for the year to March 31, 1997 had fallen to 8.6 million stg after an exceptional charge of 13.5 million compared with a profit of 28.6 million in the previous year.

The charge will be used to rationalise its European fluorescent light fittings manufacturing capacity through the planned closure of its factory in Germany. It also plans to close other smaller manufacturing activities in Europe and Australia.
TLG, which was spun off from Thorn EMI in 1994, said that the continued strength of the pound would continue to have an impact on performance.
The company maintained its total dividend payout at 4.3p per share.
